prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation: approved-limit supply; observation never replaces protection/control/local verification. Bay Automation Controller (Juniper): distinct North Bay Controller/South Bay Controller scopes; validate mode/interlocks/authority/availability; ordered/hold/stop sequences, shared-equipment coordination, indication comparison, abnormal/stale-point reporting; Breaker Inspection Tag context; sends timestamped Bay Status Digest to Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing); receives Battery Load Test Record from Station DC System. North blocks unready closing, preserves approved local control during communications loss; South reports mode/availability. Breaker Control Unit: authorized/interlocked outputs/tests, position/health returns, local authority precedence. Glasswing: authorized interface, quality/staleness, Alarm Acknowledgement Slip, cleared history, recovery validation; receives Protocol Retry Summary from Station Gateway, which brokers mapped/authorized traffic, rejects malformed/stale/unauthorized requests, reports faults without equipment changes. Control Room Operator: reviews alarms/equipment/restrictions, records actions, produces Clearance Handoff Memo, verifies handback; acknowledgement/clearing proves no correction. Uncertain status/missing permissives inhibit remote commands; degraded communications make indications unavailable pending validation; layers remain independent.
Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem): independent approved-setting trips; Relay Diagnostic Note. North Protection Panel: independent feeder protection; Transformer Protection Panel: independent transformer protection/local reporting. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur): investigations, independently approved/validated settings; discrepancies block release; pretest scope/settings/restoration review. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin): quality/holdover; Clock Drift Snapshot to Sequence Event Archive (Orchard): ordered/uncertain/corrected histories, testing/restoration events, auditable retention/export/recovery. Station DC System: monitored supply; loss abnormal. Engineering Workstation: authorized configuration/revision review, Settings Review Receipt to Maintenance Remote Terminal; controlled sessions/no bypass.
Substation Supervisor: authorization/escalation/change control; coordinates timing/responsibilities with Switching Desk Coordinator, who confirms prerequisites/current sequence. Substation Field Crew (Cinder): local indication/discrepancy verification; confirmed clearances/isolation/grounding/boundaries; reports unsafe conditions. Maintenance considers loading/switching/staffing. Tests require approved procedures/calibrated instruments/stop means; preserve energized-feeder protection; operator tracks disabled functions through verified restoration. Manual operation requires approved procedures/local checks/operator communication.

New part:
S218: A suspected controller or relay fault is assessed before any restart, bypass, or replacement is attempted.
S219: Restoration includes confirming normal indications, protection availability, communications status, and the removal of temporary test connections.
S220: The Substation Supervisor confirms that required records are complete and that operating restrictions are formally cleared before returning equipment to normal service.
S221: Operational assurance at Alder Creek depends on clear authority, verified equipment state, and records that support later review.
S222: The Control Room Operator remains responsible for deciding whether an automation request is appropriate for current operating conditions.
S223: The Bay Automation Controller shall execute only commands permitted by its approved logic and configured interlocks.
S224: The Feeder Protection Relay shall retain its protective function independently of supervisory communications.
S225: The Protection Relay Engineer reviews protection behavior after material changes and records any unresolved concerns for operational follow-up.
S226: The Station Supervisory Control System presents control indications and command results for operator assessment.
S227: The Sequence Event Archive retains time-ordered records needed to reconstruct significant control and protection events.
S228: The Engineering Workstation shall be used for authorized configuration work under established change control.
S229: The Satellite Time Receiver supports consistent event timing, and time-quality concerns shall be investigated before records are relied upon for sequence analysis.
S230: The Station Gateway shall maintain the defined boundary between station automation and external communications.
S231: The Station DC System shall be confirmed available before switching that depends on station control power.
S232: The Breaker Control Unit shall reject commands that do not satisfy its configured permissive conditions.
S233: Substation Field Crew uses the Isolation Boundary Card to verify the approved work boundary before entering the controlled area.
S234: Substation Field Crew reports unexpected equipment conditions promptly and pauses work when the approved boundary is uncertain.
S235: Switching Desk Coordinator receives the Clearance Handoff Memo and confirms that its clearance status agrees with the active switching record.
S236: Keystone shall confirm that switching authority, equipment state, and communication limits are understood before coordinating any automation-enabled action.
S237: The Substation Supervisor verifies that unresolved risks have an assigned owner and an agreed disposition before normal service is resumed.
S238: The Control Room Operator confirms indications locally when remote status is incomplete, inconsistent, or delayed.
S239: The Protection Relay Engineer assesses unexplained trips and abnormal protection indications before protection is returned to service.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
